data.confirm: I know this system is not recommended and accept it

data_description.control: TPI + PWM: switches the relay in pulses (on for a share of every cycle) by the error and the heat need – fits most relay boilers. PID + PWM: the same pulses with an integral, it does not stay below the target. External thermostat: HC only sets the target of an existing thermostat (a TRV, Better Thermostat, a Wi-Fi heater). AC – virtual i-Feel: HC moves the air conditioner's setpoint so that the room thermometer (not the unit's own sensor) reaches the target. On/off: plain on below / off above the target with long runs (heat pumps). Heating curve: flow temperature by the outdoor temperature.

entities.title: Entities
entities.description: A new instance always starts in shadow mode: it calculates but switches nothing. Only the fields on top are needed, the More part can be set later; where possible, I filled them in.

data.indoor_entity: Indoor temperature (optional when a wall thermostat contact is given)
data.actuator_entity: Switched relay (the boiler, or for a zone its zone valve / room relay)
data.flow_setpoint_entity: Flow setpoint entity (number / input_number, e.g. OpenTherm or ebusd)
data.demand_entity: Wired wall thermostat contact (optional: on = it asks for heat)

data_description.floor_entity: The thermometer in the floor. Required for electric floor heating: without it, or without a fresh reading, it does not heat.
data_description.demand_entity: A dry-contact wall thermostat read through a binary sensor, input boolean or switch: on = heat, off = no heat; then the room thermometer is optional. Frost, window, summer rest, the floor limit and floor tempering still apply. Unavailable: the lost-sensor fallback.

more.name: More (optional)
more.description: Meters, a second heat source, floor, heat pump, target source. They can be set later in the settings too.

data.energy_factor: Heat per unit (Custom only: kWh per metered unit)
data.extra_heat_entity: Other heat source energy (cumulative, e.g. air conditioner)
data.extra_factor: Heat per unit of the other source (e.g. COP)
data.boiler_power_kw: Boiler output (0 = heat need is not used in regulation)
data.zone_temp_entity: Adjoining room thermometer (e.g. a conservatory or the next room)
data.zone_max_diff: Counts as part of the house if at most this much colder
data.valve_feedback_entity: Valve feedback (end switch or valve position, if there is one)
data.floor_max: Floor temperature limit (0 = by covering and probe position)
data.floor_hysteresis: Back on this far below the limit
data.onoff_hysteresis: Switch on this far below the target
data.power_available_entity: Controlled power signal (optional: on = power available)
data.floor_temper: Floor tempering (keep the floor warm even when the room is warm enough)
data.floor_temper_offset: Floor target above the room target (0 = by the floor covering)
data.floor_temper_night: Floor target at night / in the sleep preset (0 = as by day)
data.floor_temper_hysteresis: Tempering back on this far below the floor target
data.floor_temper_room_margin: No tempering once the room is this much above its target
data.floor_fallback: Lost room thermometer: keep the floor warm by the floor sensor
data.heat_fuel: Fuel (the heat is worked out from it)

data_description.reference_entity: Used by fault detection and the shadow comparison. If empty, the relay or thermostat.
data_description.heat_energy_entity: The heat need is learned from these and the temperatures. It needs at least 3 whole days, statistics count too.
data_description.extra_factor: Heat per metered unit of the other source: for a heat pump or AC its COP (3 = 1 kWh of power gives 3 kWh of heat).
data_description.valve_feedback_entity: The central boiler uses it to see whether the valve is really open (on/off, open/closed or at least 20 %). Empty or unavailable: it counts with the actuator opening time.
data_description.floor_entity: The thermometer in the floor. Required for electric floor heating: without it, or without a fresh reading, it does not heat.
data_description.floor_max: No heat above it, whatever the regulator says. 0 = by the covering and the sensor position: under the covering 29 °C for tiles, 27 °C for wood, laminate, vinyl, carpet; in the screed between the pipes 29 / 33 / 31 (vinyl) °C; above a supply pipe 36 °C. An electric floor always uses the under-covering value. Without a covering: 27 °C for an electric floor, 29 °C for a water floor.
data_description.target_source_entity: When someone changes its target (e.g. on the wall thermostat's knob), this instance takes it over as a manual target until the next scheduled change. What HC writes there itself is not taken over.
data_description.hp_defrost_entity: While on (or named defrost), fault detection waits and the run does not count as running without command.
data_description.hp_dhw_entity: A 3-way valve or a mode sensor: while it makes hot water the house waits, this is no fault.
data_description.floor_temper: Comfort: a warm floor. While the room is warm enough the floor is held at the room target + the offset (by the floor sensor); it stops when the room gets this much above its target. The floor limit always wins. Needs a floor sensor.
data_description.floor_temper_room_margin: Default 0.5 °C. A larger value gives a warmer floor, but the room swings further above its target and uses more energy.
data_description.floor_fallback: Instead of the blind demand (or, for an electric floor, no heat) the floor is held at the room target + the tempering offset while the room thermometer is silent. Without a floor reading it works as before.
data_description.floor_covering: Gives the floor limit (with the sensor position) and the tempering offset: tiles 2 °C, other coverings 3 °C.
data_description.floor_probe: A sensor deeper in the screed reads warmer than the surface, so its limit is higher. The deeper positions' limits (screed 31–33 °C, above a pipe 36 °C) are estimates: they do not guarantee a surface below 27 °C. Under wood, parquet and laminate a sensor right under the covering (surface) is recommended.
data_description.heat_fuel: Automatic: from the meter's unit (m³ gas, kWh, MJ, GJ), without a meter from the heat source. Custom: the number below is kept. For a heat pump, Custom is right.
data_description.heat_efficiency: Counts for a burner (gas, oil, pellet); not for electric heat or a heat meter.
data_description.gas_heating_value: kWh/m³, used for natural gas only (Automatic with a meter in m³, or Natural gas). 9.61 is the Hungarian bills' 34.6 MJ/m³; elsewhere use the value on your bill (MJ/m³ ÷ 3.6).

central.title: Central boiler
central.description: Switches the boiler by the demand of the chosen zone thermostats; waits for actuator valves to open. Starts in shadow mode. With a modulating boiler, the zone asking the most sets the flow by its own curve.

data.confirm: I understand: active mode switches a real device
data.central_keep_alive_s: Resend the boiler's on state every (s, 0 = off)
data.central_pump_overrun_s: Pump overrun after the boiler stops (0 = off)
data.central_pump_bypass: Bypass / always-open circuit (the overrun needs no open valve)
data.flow_setpoint_entity: Flow setpoint (modulating boiler, optional: number / input_number)
data.central_flow_default: Flow when no zone asks for a value
data.central_pump_exercise_s: Weekly pump exercise: run time (0 = off)
data.central_pump_exercise_idle_days: Only when the pump has stood still for (days)

data_description.central_pump_exercise_s: With a pump entity: a pump that stood still for days runs alone for this long once a week, so it does not seize. Only while the boiler is off and no zone asks; the boiler does not start; not in the first minutes after a restart.

buffer.title: Buffer tank
buffer.description: Switches the heat source (pellet, heat pump, electric element) by the tank thermometers: the top below the lower limit starts it, the tank charges up to the upper limit. With zones given a new charge only starts while a zone asks for heat. Starts in shadow mode. Up to four thermometers (top, upper, lower, bottom) and the volume give the stored heat, the charge and the trend – information only, the charging still goes by the top and the bottom.

data.boiler_entity: Heat source relay (optional: empty = HC only watches the tank)
data.buffer_demand_led: Start a new charge only on zone demand
data.buffer_on: Charge starts when the top is this cold or colder
data.buffer_off: Charge stops when the bottom (or the top) reaches
data.buffer_frost: Frost: charge when the top falls below
data.buffer_base_temp: Base: water below this heats nothing
data.buffer_share_top: Share of the top layer (0 = even)
data.buffer_share_upper: Share of the upper-middle layer (0 = even)
data.buffer_share_lower: Share of the lower-middle layer (0 = even)
data.buffer_share_bottom: Share of the bottom layer (0 = even)
data.buffer_charge_entity: Existing charge percentage of the tank (taken over unchanged, optional)
data.dhw_pump_entity: Hot water tank charging pump (optional, drawing only)
data.dhw_temp_entity: Hot water tank thermometer (optional, drawing only)
data.dhw_heater_entity: Hot water tank electric heater (PV / grid; optional, drawing only)

data_description.buffer_top_entity: The tank's topmost thermometer – the start of a charge and what the circuits can get go by it.
data_description.buffer_bottom_entity: When given, a charge stops when the bottom is warm too (a full charge). Without it the top decides.
data_description.boiler_entity: The switch that starts the source charging the tank (pellet, electric element). For a heat pump the heat pump coordination does it – leave this empty.
data_description.zone_entities: The HC zones heated from the tank. With them a charge starts only while one asks for heat (see below).
data_description.buffer_demand_led: On: no charging "for later" – a new charge starts only with a zone demand. The frost limit always charges.
data_description.buffer_on: When the top cools to this, a charge starts. Keep it above what the circuits need.
data_description.buffer_off: The end of a charge. For a heat pump not above what it can reach through the coil.
data_description.buffer_min_off_s: At least this pause between two charges, so the source does not cycle.
data_description.buffer_max_charge_s: A charge running longer is stopped and reported (a faulty sensor, a weak source).
data_description.buffer_frost: Under this it always charges, even when no zone asks.
data_description.buffer_upper_entity: For a truer picture of a stratified tank (stored heat, charge). It switches nothing.
data_description.buffer_lower_entity: For a truer picture of a stratified tank; the heat pump's demand-based charging stops by this layer by default.
data_description.buffer_volume_l: With it HC also works in kWh (stored heat, reserve above the need).
data_description.buffer_base_temp: 0 % charge: water colder than this no longer heats. ~30 °C for radiators, ~25 °C for floor heating.
data_description.buffer_share_top: The share of the tank around this thermometer. 0 = equal among the given thermometers.
data_description.buffer_charge_entity: When your controller already works out a charge, HC shows that instead of its own.
data_description.dhw_pump_entity: The pump charging the hot water tank from the buffer – shown on the diagram only, HC does not switch it.
data_description.dhw_temp_entity: On the diagram and the overview only.
data_description.dhw_heater_entity: On the diagram and the overview only.

basics.description: Targets and timing; they can be changed in the options any time.

data_description.valve_delay_s: When the zone valve opens slowly (thermoelectric, ~5 minutes) or the pump is started late by its own control: heat starts this long after switching on. HC lengthens the run by it, the minimum on time counts the useful part, and demands too small for a run are carried into the next cycles. 0 = no delay.
data_description.min_on_s: The shortest useful run; with a delay set, a smaller demand is carried into the next cycle.

circuit.title: Mixing circuit
circuit.description: A radiator or floor circuit with its own pump and mixing valve, fed from a buffer tank. HC works out the flow target from the outdoor temperature and the lasting demand of its zones and gives out a target that changes only now and then. It starts in shadow mode (writes nothing); writing – a supervised trial or active – is switched on in its settings.

data.circuit_buffer: Buffer tank instance it draws from
data.circuit_output_entity: Where the flow target is written (PLC number / input_number / climate, optional)
data.circuit_pump_entity: The circuit's pump runs (PLC signal, optional, display only)
data.circuit_flow_entity: The circuit's measured flow temperature (optional, display only)

data_description.circuit_kind: Radiator or floor: different curve, limits and steps by default (set on the next page).
data_description.zone_entities: The HC zones (rooms) on this circuit. The target comes from the targets and deficits of the zones with a lasting demand.
data_description.outdoor_entity: The heating curve's outdoor temperature. When it is lost, the given-out target stays.
data_description.circuit_buffer: With it you see the heat the tank still has for the circuit, the heat pump knows its need, and the tank cap can be switched on.
data_description.circuit_output_entity: The PLC's flow setpoint. Nothing is written in shadow; the mixer, pump and protections stay with the PLC.
data_description.circuit_pump_entity: When the PLC reports it, the drawing shows the real pump state.
data_description.circuit_flow_entity: The real flow next to the given-out target – to check the mixer.

circuit_settings.title: Mixing circuit – curve and hold
circuit_settings.description:
The defaults depend on the circuit type. The maximum is the water's flow limit, not the floor surface limit – that protection stays on the hydraulic / PLC side.

**The curve of these values** (at the room target, within the limits):

{curve}

Tick *Preview only* and submit to recompute the table without saving.

data.circuit_room: Fallback room temperature (no zone has a target)
data.circuit_kp: Room correction (°C of water per °C of room deficit)
data.circuit_dt: Flow − return at design (for the usable heat of the tank)
data.circuit_margin: Tank top above the flow target at least
data.circuit_hold_s: A zone that asked within this has a lasting demand
data.circuit_idle_keep: Keep the zones' target in a pause (no drop)
data.circuit_deadband: New target only for a difference of at least
data.circuit_max_rise: Rise at most per change (0 = no limit)
data.circuit_preview: Preview only: shows the curve of the values entered, saves nothing
data.circuit_tank_cap: Circuit target at most the tank's top − margin
data.circuit_room_trim: Flow from the rooms' lasting shortfall
data.circuit_watch_flow_c: This much change counts as moving

data_description.circuit_tank_cap: Off by default, so an update never changes a live PLC setpoint by itself. On: the target given to the mixer = min(demanded, tank top − tank margin). A cooling tank lowers it at once, a warming one lets it back up step by step. The heat pump still gets the uncapped need. A cap below the minimum keeps the minimum and warns "tank too cold"; without a tank reading the last good one caps for 15 minutes, then nothing caps.
data_description.circuit_slope: °C of water per degree between the room target and outdoors. Radiators ~1.0–1.5, floor ~0.3–0.6.
data_description.circuit_shift: Moves the whole curve up (+) or down (−). If it is always too cold or warm, set this first.
data_description.circuit_room: Only when no zone has a target (e.g. all are off).
data_description.circuit_flow_max: The water's flow limit. The floor surface protection stays with the PLC / hydraulics.
data_description.circuit_kp: A room with a lasting demand under its target asks for this much warmer water per degree (up to 3 °C deficit).
data_description.circuit_dt: The circuit's design temperature drop: for estimating the tank's usable heat.
data_description.circuit_margin: The heat pump asks for a tank this much warmer than the target; with the tank cap on, the mixer gets at most top − this.
data_description.circuit_hold_s: A short TPI pause does not end the demand: a request within this time still counts.
data_description.circuit_idle_keep: On: the target does not drop to the 20 °C fallback in a pause; the pump enable is a separate signal.
data_description.circuit_deadband: No new target for small wobbles.
data_description.circuit_confirm_s: The difference must last this long before a new target goes out.
data_description.circuit_min_interval_s: At least this long between two changes, so the mixer does not keep moving.
data_description.circuit_max_rise: Rises step by step; no limit going down.
data_description.circuit_urgent: A difference this large does not wait for the confirmation and the interval.
data_description.circuit_room_trim: Weighed every hour: when most of the circuit's rooms heated nearly all the time and still stayed below their targets, the flow rises by the step below; when all held their targets easily, heating less than half the time, it goes down. Kept over a restart. Off by default: it moves the mixer's live target.
data_description.circuit_trim_step: Up or down by this much after each weighing.
data_description.circuit_trim_s: The rooms are watched this long before a step.
data_description.circuit_trim_max: The flow differs from the curve by at most this much.
data_description.circuit_watch: Watching only: it writes nothing and does not touch the PLC. When the circuit asks for heat the pump (PLC) should start within the time below, then the flow should move or get near the target. When a step is missing, HC puts an entry in Repairs. It needs the pump and the flow thermometer entities; with only one of them, that step is watched.
data_description.circuit_watch_pump_s: Leave room for the PLC's own start delay (for example 5 minutes); waiting until then is normal.
data_description.circuit_watch_flow_s: Counted from the pump's start. When by then the flow has neither moved nor got near the target (within 2 °C), it is a problem (a stuck mixer, a cold tank, a stopped valve controller).
data_description.circuit_watch_flow_c: The flow should change this much from the pump's start.

hp_coord.title: Heat pump coordination
hp_coord.description: For a heat pump charging a buffer tank (through its coil or directly), beside other sources such as a wood boiler. HC works out the ON/OFF request, the heat demand and a rarely changing flow target with your offset, from the buffer, its mixing circuits and the outdoor temperature. It starts in shadow mode (writes nothing); writing – a supervised trial or active – is switched on in its settings.

data.hp_running_entity: Heat pump runs now (optional: binary, climate, or a number with its unit: W, kW, A, Hz, rpm, %)
data.wood_entity: Wood boiler signal (optional: on while it fires)
data.hp_target_entity: Where the flow target is written (number / input_number / climate, optional)
data.hp_switch_entity: Heat pump ON/OFF (switch / input_boolean / climate, optional)
data.hp_summer_entity: Summer mode signal for a PLC (switch / input_boolean, optional)
data.hp_exercise_entity: Exercise due signal for a PLC (switch / input_boolean, optional)
data.wood_temp_entity: Wood boiler thermometer (instead of a direct signal; two thresholds)
data.hp_water_temp_entity: The heat pump's measured water temperature (optional)

data_description.hp_target_round: HC keeps its decimals inside; this is only the value sent to the heat pump. Up to whole °C: 36.1 → 37 °C.
data_description.hp_water_temp_entity: Only for the "Heat pump target" chart: how the water follows the given-out target.
data_description.hp_buffer: The tank instance the heat pump charges – its temperatures, layers and circuits come from there.
data_description.outdoor_entity: The cold-weather ON and the summer / winter mode go by it.
data_description.hp_running_entity: With a power (W) or frequency reading HC decides itself whether it runs. Needed to recognise wood.
data_description.wood_entity: A direct signal (flue thermostat, boiler relay): while it is on the heat pump does not charge.
data_description.wood_temp_entity: Without a direct signal: burning is told from the wood boiler's thermometer by two thresholds (on the rules page).
data_description.hp_target_entity: The heat pump's flow target. Its rounding is set below.
data_description.hp_switch_entity: The ON / OFF request. ON is no heating command: with no demand the target is the lowest.
data_description.hp_demand_entity: A switch telling the PLC that heat is wanted now.
data_description.hp_summer_entity: Tells the PLC it is summer mode.
data_description.hp_exercise_entity: In summer mode it tells the PLC weekly to run the pumps and valves.

hp_coord_settings.title: Heat pump coordination – rules
hp_coord_settings.description: Flow target = the circuits' need + reserve + offset, within the limits (after the offset). The cold-weather ON is only for a water-filled monoblock and never replaces its own frost protection; it wins over the long no-demand stop.

data.hp_flow_min: Lowest flow target (also the standby target)
data.hp_reserve: Tank / coil reserve above the circuits' need
data.hp_offset: Manual offset (also adjustable any time with the "Offset" number entity)
data.hp_hyst: Stop only this much above the need
data.hp_charge_on: Start at or below this charge (0 = not used)
data.hp_charge_off: Stop only at or above this charge (0 = not used)
data.hp_charge_needs_demand: The charge starts / keeps a heating only while a room or circuit asks
data.hp_standby: Keep ON with no demand (standby, lowest target)
data.hp_idle_off: OFF after a long time without demand
data.hp_auto_summer: Automatic summer / winter mode (by the house's demand)
data.hp_summer_after_h: Summer mode after this long without demand
data.hp_winter_after_s: Back to winter when the circuits' demand lasted this long (0 = at once)
data.hp_exercise: Exercise due signal in summer mode (the PLC runs it)
data.hp_wood_rise: Tank warming that means another source (°C/h)
data.hp_wood_first: Wood first: also no low-charge start, and a running heating stops (frost protection and cold-weather ON stay)
data.hp_deadband: New target only for a difference of at least
data.hp_max_rise: Rise at most per change (0 = no limit)
data.wood_on_above: Wood active when the boiler is at least
data.wood_off_below: Wood inactive when the boiler is at most
data.wood_confirm_s: Lasting this long before it changes
data.hp_start_kwh: Demand: start when the heat reserve drops below (kWh, 0 = not used)
data.hp_stop_layer: Demand: the layer that decides the stop
data.hp_coil_dt: Demand: coil temperature step (the tank stays this much under the heat pump's target)
data.hp_lead_min: Demand: start by the pace of use (minutes ahead, 0 = off)
data.hp_running_w: The compressor runs above this many watts
data.hp_standby_w: Standby above this many watts (the compressor stands)
data.hp_charge_jump: Full target at once for a new charge

data_description.hp_charge_mode: Classic: starts when the tank top drops under the need or the charge under its threshold; by demand: the top must stay above need + start margin, and it stops only when the chosen layer reaches need + stop margin too. Both are always worked out and shown in HC info, so they can be compared in shadow.
data_description.hp_flow_min: This is the target with no demand (standby).
data_description.hp_flow_max: It never asks the heat pump for more.
data_description.hp_reserve: The heat pump's target = the circuits' need + this + offset. Needed for the coil's heat transfer.
data_description.hp_offset: A manual shift of −8…+8 °C when the unit's own reading differs from the tank.
data_description.hp_hyst: Classic: a charge stops when the top is at least need + this.
data_description.hp_charge_on: Classic: starts on a low charge even while the top is still warm enough.
data_description.hp_charge_off: Classic: a charge may stop only above this.
data_description.hp_charge_needs_demand: Classic: a low charge alone starts nothing, only with a room or circuit asking.
data_description.hp_start_margin: Starts while the top still has this much reserve above the need – the coil's heat reaches the top slowly.
data_description.hp_start_kwh: With the tank's volume: also starts when the heat above the need falls under this.
data_description.hp_stop_layer: It stops only when this layer reaches need + stop margin too. Without a thermometer there, the one above counts.
data_description.hp_stop_margin: How far above the need the stop layer must be.
data_description.hp_coil_dt: Through the coil the tank gets this much colder water than the target – the stop never waits for more.
data_description.hp_min_on_s: Compressor protection: stays ON at least this long.
data_description.hp_min_off_s: Compressor protection: stays OFF at least this long.
data_description.hp_standby: Stays ON with the lowest target when nothing is needed (e.g. a unit that protects itself only while ON).
data_description.hp_idle_off: In standby: switches OFF after a long time with no demand.
data_description.hp_idle_hours: After this many hours with no demand.
data_description.hp_auto_summer: Not by date: summer mode after a long time with no room demand; back to winter on the circuits' lasting demand.
data_description.hp_summer_after_h: Summer mode after this many hours with no demand.
data_description.hp_winter_after_s: One TPI pulse or airing does not bring the heating back.
data_description.hp_exercise: Signals weekly in summer mode; the PLC runs the pumps.
data_description.hp_exercise_min: How long the signal lasts, in minutes.
data_description.hp_cold_on: Only for a water-filled monoblock: stays ON in frost so the unit's own frost protection can work. It does not replace it.
data_description.hp_cold_release_s: …when it stays above for this long.
data_description.hp_wood_rise: If the tank warms faster than this while the heat pump does not run, HC takes it as wood burning.
data_description.hp_wood_first: On: no heat pump charging while wood burns (frost and cold-weather ON stay).
data_description.wood_on_above: Wood boiler thermometer above this: burning.
data_description.wood_off_below: …and under this: out. The band between stops flapping.
data_description.wood_confirm_s: It must last this long before it switches.
data_description.hp_deadband: No new target for small wobbles.
data_description.hp_confirm_s: The difference must last this long.
data_description.hp_min_interval_s: At least this long between two changes.
data_description.hp_urgent: A difference this large does not wait.
data_description.hp_lead_min: When the tank cools steadily (at least 0.2 °C/h) and at that pace its top would fall under the need within this many minutes, it starts now – the coil's heat takes time to reach the top.
data_description.hp_running_w: When the "runs" signal is a power meter, above this many W it counts as running (100 W by default).
data_description.hp_standby_w: When the run signal is a power meter: above this but below the compressor's threshold the heat pump is in standby (switched on, for frost protection or circulation for example, but the compressor stands). Below it, it stands. It only makes the display exact; for the coordination standby is "does not run", as before.
data_description.hp_charge_jump: When a charge starts, and when the compressor stops below the target during a charge, the given-out target goes straight to the worked-out value; the hold only smooths changes within a charge.

data.hp_stop_layer: Demand: the layer that decides the stop
data.hp_coil_dt: Demand: coil temperature step (the tank stays this much under the heat pump's target)
data.hp_lead_min: Demand: start by the pace of use (minutes ahead, 0 = off)

data_description.hp_start_margin: Starts while the top still has this much reserve above the need – the coil's heat reaches the top slowly.
data_description.hp_start_kwh: With the tank's volume: also starts when the heat above the need falls under this.
data_description.hp_stop_layer: It stops only when this layer reaches need + stop margin too. Without a thermometer there, the one above counts.
data_description.hp_stop_margin: How far above the need the stop layer must be.
data_description.hp_coil_dt: Through the coil the tank gets this much colder water than the target – the stop never waits for more.
data_description.hp_lead_min: When the tank cools steadily (at least 0.2 °C/h) and at that pace its top would fall under the need within this many minutes, it starts now – the coil's heat takes time to reach the top.

data.hp_hyst: Stop only this much above the need
data.hp_charge_on: Start at or below this charge (0 = not used)
data.hp_charge_off: Stop only at or above this charge (0 = not used)
data.hp_charge_needs_demand: The charge starts / keeps a heating only while a room or circuit asks

data_description.hp_hyst: Classic: a charge stops when the top is at least need + this.
data_description.hp_charge_on: Classic: starts on a low charge even while the top is still warm enough.
data_description.hp_charge_off: Classic: a charge may stop only above this.
data_description.hp_charge_needs_demand: Classic: a low charge alone starts nothing, only with a room or circuit asking.

data.hp_idle_off: OFF after a long time without demand
data.hp_running_w: The compressor runs above this many watts

data_description.hp_min_off_s: Compressor protection: stays OFF at least this long.
data_description.hp_standby: Stays ON with the lowest target when nothing is needed (e.g. a unit that protects itself only while ON).
data_description.hp_idle_off: In standby: switches OFF after a long time with no demand.
data_description.hp_idle_hours: After this many hours with no demand.

Below it, it stands. It only makes the display exact; for the coordination standby is "does not run", as before.

data.hp_summer_after_h: Summer mode after this long without demand

data.hp_exercise: Exercise due signal in summer mode (the PLC runs it)

data_description.hp_auto_summer: Not by date: summer mode after a long time with no room demand; back to winter on the circuits' lasting demand.

data_description.hp_winter_after_s: One TPI pulse or airing does not bring the heating back.
data_description.hp_exercise: Signals weekly in summer mode; the PLC runs the pumps.
data_description.hp_exercise_min: How long the signal lasts, in minutes.

data_description.hp_cold_on: Only for a water-filled monoblock: stays ON in frost so the unit's own frost protection can work. It does not replace it.
data_description.hp_cold_release_s: …when it stays above for this long.

data.hp_wood_rise: Tank warming that means another source (°C/h)
data.hp_wood_first: Wood first: also no low-charge start, and a running heating stops (frost protection and cold-weather ON stay)
data.wood_on_above: Wood active when the boiler is at least
data.wood_off_below: Wood inactive when the boiler is at most
data.wood_confirm_s: Lasting this long before it changes

data_description.hp_wood_rise: If the tank warms faster than this while the heat pump does not run, HC takes it as wood burning.
data_description.hp_wood_first: On: no heat pump charging while wood burns (frost and cold-weather ON stay).
data_description.wood_on_above: Wood boiler thermometer above this: burning.
data_description.wood_off_below: …and under this: out. The band between stops flapping.
data_description.wood_confirm_s: It must last this long before it switches.

data.hp_deadband: New target only for a difference of at least
data.hp_max_rise: Rise at most per change (0 = no limit)
data.hp_charge_jump: Full target at once for a new charge

data_description.hp_deadband: No new target for small wobbles.

data_description.hp_min_interval_s: At least this long between two changes.
data_description.hp_urgent: A difference this large does not wait.
data_description.hp_charge_jump: When a charge starts, and when the compressor stops below the target during a charge, the given-out target goes straight to the worked-out value; the hold only smooths changes within a charge.

go_live.title: Go live: {name}
go_live.description:
In shadow mode HC calculates and logs what it would do, but switches nothing. Live, it switches the boiler relay (or sets the thermostat / AC unit, the TRV heads) itself.

Go live only when the shadow decisions looked right for a while and nothing else (a wall thermostat, an automation) controls the same output. Every other setting stays as it is.

go_shadow.description: HC keeps calculating and logging, but switches nothing from now on. The output stays as it is now – switch it by hand if needed.

data_description.target_home: At home and awake. Also settable from the thermostat card.
data_description.target_night: Between the night's start and end (below), and in the Sleep preset.
data_description.target_away: When nobody is home (by the presence entities) or in the Away preset.
data_description.target_vacation: In the Vacation preset – a short absence keeps the Away target.
data_description.frost_temp: It never cools below this, not even while off or with a window open.
data_description.night_start: The sleep target applies from this time.
data_description.night_end: The sleep target lasts until this; optimal start times itself to it.
data_description.mode: Shadow: works out only, to compare with the current control. Active: HC switches the device.
data_description.confirm: Must be ticked for active mode: nothing else may drive the same output.
data_description.night_start_weekend: For Friday and Saturday evening's night (ending on Saturday and Sunday morning). Empty: as on weekdays. Give both the start and the end.
data_description.night_end_weekend: On Saturday and Sunday morning the sleep target lasts until this – e.g. 08:00 if you sleep longer at the weekend.

regulation.name: Control and timing
regulation.description: Controller, cycle, minimum times, start holds, PID and curve parameters.

data.coast_window_s: Wait for the after-heat after a burn (0 = off)
data.pre_change_s: No new start before the target goes down (0 = off)
data.yield_margin: While the other (cheaper) source heats the coupled zone, the boiler regulates this much below the target (0 = off)
data.pid_ki_per_hour: PID integral gain (demand per °C per hour)
data.room_ki_per_hour: Room correction slow part (°C per °C per hour)
data.onoff_hysteresis: Switch on this far below the target
data.ac_ki_per_hour: AC: slow setpoint correction (°C per °C per hour)
data.ac_min_change_s: AC: minimum time between setpoint changes
data.assist_climate: House thermostat the AC helps when cheaper and the door is open (HC)
data.assist_delay_s: Help only after the door has been open this long
data.assist_max_setpoint: The unit's setpoint while helping at most
data.storage_discharge_hyst: Discharge starts this far below the target
data.fan_overrun_s: Fan overrun after the valve closes
data.fan_min_coil: The fan starts only above this coil temperature
data.keep_alive_s: Resend the on state every (s, 0 = off) – for a relay with its own auto-off timer
data.catchup_gap: Fast catch-up: from this shortfall (0 = off)
data.catchup_release: Fast catch-up ends: this far below the target

data_description.control: TPI: proportional pulses by the error and the outdoor temperature. PID: proportional + integral (+ derivative) – removes a lasting offset. Both drive the relay by PWM: on for a share of every cycle.
data_description.cycle_s: PWM cycle: one on + off period. The demand is the share of it the relay is on (50 % of 900 s = 7.5 minutes on).
data_description.min_on_s: Shortest burn: a shorter pulse is skipped or stretched (spares the boiler and the relay).
data_description.valve_delay_s: A slow thermoelectric valve (~5 min) or a pump started late: the run is lengthened by it, the minimum on time counts the useful part, small demands add up. 0 = none.
data_description.coast_window_s: For this long after a burn no new start while the room, just under the target, still rises (the radiators give their heat). Suggested: 2700 s. Off by default (measured on one house).
data_description.pwm_midcycle_start: When the demand grows past the minimum run in the middle of a cycle, a new cycle starts at once (no wait for the next). Off by default (measured on one house).
data_description.pwm_carry: Demands below the minimum run add up to a real run (always so with a valve delay). Off by default: in the simulation it raised the overshoot after a boost.
data_description.pre_change_s: This long before a scheduled lowering of the target (night start, a preset or manual target running out) no new burn starts while the room is already at or above the coming target – its heat would arrive after the change. A running burn is not cut. Default: 1800 s. On a floor the default is 7200 s, because the floor gives the last hours' heat after the change. With the house's time constant known, the room may sag at most the allowed amount below in this time.
data_description.pid_kp: How strongly HC answers the error now (0.4 = 40 % demand per °C below the target).
data_description.pid_ki_per_hour: How fast a lasting error adds demand (per °C and hour).
data_description.pid_d_filter_s: Room sensors report in 0.1 °C steps, only on a change: an unfiltered derivative is spiky. 0 = no filter; only matters when the derivative gain is not 0.
data_description.keep_alive_script: When set, at every keep-alive of the relay that should stay on HC runs this script instead of switching the relay on again – for example a Shelly "turn on with a 15-minute flip-back timer". A long burn is then never cut, while a dead Home Assistant leaves the relay on for that long at most.
data_description.min_off_s: Stays off at least this long after switching off (protects boiler and relay).
data_description.pid_kd: Damps fast changes. 0 = none; only if the temperature overshoots.
data_description.curve_slope: °C of water per degree between the target and outdoors.
data_description.curve_shift: Moves the whole curve up (+) or down (−) – if always too cold or warm, set this first.
data_description.flow_min: It never asks for colder flow.
data_description.flow_max: It never asks for warmer flow (low for floor heating, for the surface).
data_description.room_kp: Warmer water per degree the room is under its target.
data_description.room_ki_per_hour: Slowly removes a lasting offset; too large makes it swing.
data_description.onoff_hysteresis: On-off control: switches on this far under the target, off at the target.
data_description.ac_ki_per_hour: Slowly corrects the AC's target when the room stays off it.
data_description.ac_min_change_s: Changes the AC's target at most this often (beeps, wear).
data_description.assist_climate: The house's main HC thermostat: the AC helps it when cheaper and the door is open.
data_description.assist_delay_s: Helping the house starts only when the door has been open this long without a break, so a quick walk through does not raise the unit's setpoint. 0 = at once (the earlier behaviour).
data_description.assist_max_setpoint: While helping, the setpoint written to the unit is never higher than this – the unit warms its own room most. 0 = no limit (the earlier behaviour).
data_description.storage_bias: Tune it if the mornings are too warm or cold.
data_description.storage_discharge_hyst: Opens the discharge this far under the target.
data_description.fan_min_pct: The fan never runs slower while heating.
data_description.fan_overrun_s: Blows out the heat left in the coil.
data_description.fan_min_coil: No cold draught from a cold coil.
data_description.keep_alive_s: For a relay that switches itself off after a while.
data_description.yield_margin: So the boiler does not compete with the cheaper source, it regulates this far under the target.
data_description.catchup_gap: A room at least this far below its target for the time below gets the whole cycle, no PWM pause, until it is near the target. The slow learning keeps refining meanwhile.
data_description.catchup_after_s: The room must stay below the threshold this long. Floor heating: 2 hours by default, the screed still gives heat for hours.
data_description.catchup_release: Once the room is this close to the target, the TPI's proportional cycle regulates again.
data_description.tpi_coef_int: Demand per 1 °C shortfall (0.6 = 60 %). Higher: longer heating at a smaller shortfall. With learning on, the starting value.
data_description.tpi_coef_ext: Demand per degree between the target and the outdoor temperature (0.01 = 1 %/°C).

functions.name: Features
functions.description: Summer rest, boost, learning, taking over from a wall thermostat.

data.season_enabled: Summer rest by outdoor daily average
data.boost_enabled: Boost on a large deficit (accounts for after-heat)
data.learning_enabled: Learning (after-heat, boost time, TPI strength and holding offset)
data.shadow_regulator: Shadow regulator: the other algorithm (PID next to TPI) calculates too, switches nothing
data.adopt_manual: Adopt changes made on the managed thermostat
data.demand_entity: Wired wall thermostat contact (optional: on = it asks for heat)

data_description.adopt_manual: External control: a target set on the managed thermostat itself (not by HC) becomes the manual target until the next scheduled change; if someone switches it off, HC leaves it off (frost protection excepted) until someone switches it on again. Off: HC writes its own target and mode as before.
data_description.target_source_entity: When someone changes its target (e.g. on the wall thermostat's knob), this instance takes it over as a manual target until the next scheduled change. What HC writes there itself is not taken over.
data_description.demand_entity: A dry-contact wall thermostat read through a binary sensor, input boolean or switch: on = heat, off = no heat. Frost, window, summer rest, the floor limit and floor tempering still apply. Unavailable: the lost-sensor fallback.
data_description.season_off_above: When the daily outdoor mean goes above this, the heating season pauses. Default 15 °C; lower for a well insulated house, higher for an old one.
data_description.season_on_below: When the daily outdoor mean goes below this, the heating season starts again. Must be lower than the end (default 13 °C).
data_description.presence_home_states: Which values of an input_select / sensor presence source mean home (e.g. "At home"). They count besides the built-in words (home, on, otthon). With nothing here and under vacation, an unknown value writes one warning to the log.
data_description.presence_vacation_states: Which values mean vacation (e.g. "Holiday"). They count besides the built-in vacation / szabadság. Every other value is away.
data_description.season_enabled: No heating while the daily outdoor mean is above the summer limit; frost protection stays.
data_description.boost_enabled: With a large deficit it heats without pauses and stops in time, counting the learned after-heat.
data_description.learning_enabled: Learns from the house; the learned values can be reset with the reset button.
data_description.shadow_regulator: For comparison only – it does not change the decision.
data_description.ai_task_entity: When given (a Google Gemini or OpenAI AI Task, for example), HC analyses the house's heating of the previous day every morning: HC works the numbers out from the recorder (temperatures, hours below target and overheated, heating time, starts, decisions, energy and cost), the AI writes a summary, observations and things to do from them. It only advises and changes nothing. The AI button on the house drawing opens it. Empty: no daily analysis.
data_description.ai_report_time: The previous day's analysis is made at this time (06:30 by default).

protection.name: Protections
protection.description: Windows, frozen thermometer, zone valve, return limit.

data.window_drop_entities: Open window from a fast temperature drop – thermometers to watch (near the windows)
data.frozen_after_h: Frozen room thermometer: hours with an unchanged value
data.frozen_burn_min: Frozen room thermometer: minutes of heat meanwhile
data.valve_feedback_entity: Valve feedback (end switch or valve position, if there is one)
data.zone_own_mixer: Has its own mixing loop (the floor is protected whatever the boiler sends)
data.valve_exercise: Summer valve exercise (when closed for a week)
data.return_max: Return limit (0 = none): the valve stays closed above it
data.return_hysteresis: Return limit releases this far below

data_description.frozen_after_h: When the room thermometer has shown exactly the same value for this many hours while the heat ran at least the minutes below, the reading counts as frozen and the fallback runs. 0 = off. In the measured house the thermometer stayed unchanged for at most 1.4 h while heating. On a floor the default is 8 hours, and a value within 1 °C of the target is not judged: next to a slow screed the thermometer shows one value for hours while the regulation works.
data_description.frozen_burn_min: The heat must have run at least this long in the unchanged time: a real room warms by at least one step from that much heat.
data_description.valve_feedback_entity: The central boiler uses it to see whether the valve is really open (on/off, open/closed or at least 20 %). Empty or unavailable: it counts with the actuator opening time.
data_description.zone_own_mixer: Off: the flow of a central modulating boiler never goes above the highest flow of this zone (flow_max, 45 °C for a floor by default) while its circuit can get water – radiator zones heat more weakly then. Switch it on only when the floor circuit really has a mixing valve or a temperature limiter.
data_description.valve_exercise: Once a week it opens a long-closed valve for a few minutes so it does not seize. The zone asks for no heat meanwhile, a central boiler does not start.
data_description.plaus_indoor_min: Below this the room thermometer's reading counts as wrong (lost). At most the frost target minus 2 °C, so that the frost protection starts in a really cold room. Default 3 °C; lower for an unheated holiday home.
data_description.window_entities: Heating pauses while one is open (frost protection stays).
data_description.window_drop_entities: Without a window sensor: airing is told from a sudden temperature drop.
data_description.window_drop_rate: Cooling faster than this counts as airing.
data_description.exercise_weekday: Moves the valves weekly in summer too, so they do not stick.
data_description.return_max: With a condensing boiler a hot return lowers the efficiency.
data_description.return_hysteresis: Opens again this far under the limit.

floor.name: Floor (and floor cooling)
floor.description: Floor sensor, limit, tempering, dew point protection.

data.floor_max: Floor temperature limit (0 = by covering and probe position)
data.floor_hysteresis: Back on this far below the limit
data.floor_temper: Floor tempering (keep the floor warm even when the room is warm enough)
data.floor_temper_offset: Floor target above the room target (0 = by the floor covering)
data.floor_temper_night: Floor target at night / in the sleep preset (0 = as by day)
data.floor_temper_hysteresis: Tempering back on this far below the floor target
data.floor_temper_room_margin: No tempering once the room is this much above its target
data.floor_fallback: Lost room thermometer: keep the floor warm by the floor sensor
data.floor_cooling: Floor cooling in summer (reversible heat pump)
data.dew_margin: Safety margin above the dew point
data.cool_flow_entity: Cooling flow setpoint (optional; else the heating one)
data.cool_flow_max: Stop when the safe flow is warmer than this (too humid)

data_description.floor_entity: The thermometer in the floor. Required for electric floor heating: without it, or without a fresh reading, it does not heat.
data_description.floor_max: No heat above it, whatever the regulator says. 0 = by the covering and the sensor position: under the covering 29 °C for tiles, 27 °C for wood, laminate, vinyl, carpet; in the screed between the pipes 29 / 33 / 31 (vinyl) °C; above a supply pipe 36 °C. An electric floor always uses the under-covering value. Without a covering: 27 °C for an electric floor, 29 °C for a water floor.
data_description.floor_covering: Gives the floor limit (with the sensor position) and the tempering offset: tiles 2 °C, other coverings 3 °C.
data_description.floor_probe: A sensor deeper in the screed reads warmer than the surface, so its limit is higher. The deeper positions' limits (screed 31–33 °C, above a pipe 36 °C) are estimates: they do not guarantee a surface below 27 °C. Under wood, parquet and laminate a sensor right under the covering (surface) is recommended.
data_description.floor_temper: Comfort: a warm floor. While the room is warm enough the floor is held at the room target + the offset (by the floor sensor); it stops when the room gets this much above its target. The floor limit always wins. Needs a floor sensor.
data_description.floor_temper_room_margin: Default 0.5 °C. A larger value gives a warmer floor, but the room swings further above its target and uses more energy.
data_description.floor_fallback: Instead of the blind demand (or, for an electric floor, no heat) the floor is held at the room target + the tempering offset while the room thermometer is silent. Without a floor reading it works as before.
data_description.floor_cooling: In summer (heating season off) the floor cools, but the water and the floor always stay above the dew point + margin, or moisture condenses. No cooling without humidity; on/off control also needs a floor sensor.
data_description.floor_hysteresis: After the floor limit it must cool this much before heating again.
data_description.floor_temper_offset: Keeps the floor this much warmer than the room target (comfort).
data_description.floor_temper_night: A different floor target at night.
data_description.humidity_entity: For the dew point; it does not cool without it.
data_description.cool_mode_entity: The switch putting the heat pump into cooling.
data_description.dew_margin: The floor stays this far above the dew point, so no condensation.
data_description.floor_min_cool: The floor never gets colder while cooling.
data_description.cool_flow_entity: When the heat pump has its own cooling setpoint.
data_description.cool_flow_max: If the dew point would need warmer water than this, cooling stops.

devices.name: Heat source signals and power
devices.description: Burner signal, power draw, output, heat pump and electric signals.

data.flame_entity: Flame sensor (real burner state, e.g. from the boiler's power draw)
data.boiler_power_entity: Boiler power sensor (W) – for the boiler health
data.power_idle_w: Below this power the boiler stands by
data.power_burn_w: From this power the burner burns (below it only the pump runs)
data.boiler_power_kw: Boiler output (0 = heat need is not used in regulation)
data.load_limit_kw: Shared power limit of the electric zones (kW, 0 = none; the same on every zone)
data.power_available_entity: Controlled power signal (optional: on = power available)
data.hp_busy_states: Heat pump: values that mean defrost / hot water

data_description.power_idle_w: Below this the boiler stands by. Leave the defaults (20 W / 115 W) untouched and the boiler health only learns – it judges "no response" / "no flame" by the power draw once you give your boiler's own values.
data_description.power_burn_w: At or above this the burner burns (between the two: only the pump runs).
data_description.load_limit_kw: Give the zone's own power in the boiler power field (for electric heat: the heater's). If switching on would exceed the limit, the zone waits and its cycle starts later – the zones heat staggered. Counts in live mode only.
data_description.hp_defrost_entity: While on (or named defrost), fault detection waits and the run does not count as running without command.
data_description.hp_dhw_entity: A 3-way valve or a mode sensor: while it makes hot water the house waits, this is no fault.
data_description.hp_busy_states: When the defrost or hot-water signal is a mode sensor: which of its values mean the heat pump does its own work. They count besides the built-in words (on, defrost, dhw, hot_water…).
data_description.district_connection: How the flat is connected to the building's district heating: its own flat station with a heat exchanger and heat meter, or radiators straight on the risers with heat cost allocators. Only the house drawing uses it.
data_description.flame_entity: Shows whether the boiler really burns – for the fault watch and learning.
data_description.boiler_power_entity: From the power draw HC recognises burning, faults and short cycling.
data_description.boiler_power_kw: The boiler's rated heat output; for the heat-need based control.
data_description.power_available_entity: Controlled (off-peak) power: off = no power, HC does not switch.
data_description.discharge_entity: A storage heater's discharge fan or flap.
data_description.fan_entity: HC sets its speed to the heat demand.
data_description.coil_temp_entity: The fan starts only with a warm coil.

energy.name: Energy and cost
energy.description: Gas or heat meter, fuel, prices, COP.

data.heat_fuel: Fuel (the heat is worked out from it)
data.energy_factor: Heat per unit (Custom only: kWh per metered unit)
data.extra_factor: Heat per unit of the other source (e.g. COP)
data.boiler_price_entity: Boiler energy price sensor (e.g. per m³)
data.other_price_entity: Other source energy price sensor (per kWh)
data.cop_high: COP of the other source at +7 °C
data.cop_low: COP of the other source at -7 °C

data_description.heat_fuel: Automatic: from the meter's unit (m³ gas, kWh, MJ, GJ), without a meter from the heat source. Custom: the number below is kept. For a heat pump, Custom is right.
data_description.heat_efficiency: Counts for a burner (gas, oil, pellet); not for electric heat or a heat meter.
data_description.extra_factor: Heat per metered unit of the other source: for a heat pump or AC its COP (3 = 1 kWh of power gives 3 kWh of heat).
data_description.gas_heating_value: kWh/m³, used for natural gas only (Automatic with a meter in m³, or Natural gas). 9.61 is the Hungarian bills' 34.6 MJ/m³; elsewhere use the value on your bill (MJ/m³ ÷ 3.6).
data_description.heat_energy_entity: A total (increasing) value, e.g. a gas meter in m³; for the real heat use.
data_description.energy_factor: kWh of heat per meter unit (gas about 9.5–10 kWh/m³ × efficiency).
data_description.other_price_entity: For the cheaper source advice (e.g. the AC's or heat pump's electricity).
data_description.boiler_price: When there is no price sensor.
data_description.other_price: When there is no price sensor.
data_description.boiler_allowance_entity: What is left of the discounted allowance – above it, it costs more.
data_description.cop_high: Heat per 1 kWh of electricity in mild weather (+7 °C).
data_description.cop_low: Heat per 1 kWh of electricity in the cold (−7 °C).

adjoining.name: Adjoining room, shared house (several heat sources)
adjoining.description: A conservatory or the next room that gets heat through a door; and which house drawing of HC info shows this instance.

data.zone_temp_entity: Adjoining room thermometer (e.g. a conservatory or the next room)
data.zone_max_diff: Counts as part of the house if at most this much colder
data.house_link: Part of which house (HC info house drawing)

data_description.house_link: A house may have several heat sources (a boiler, an AC, an oil radiator, a heat pump), each with its own HC instance. They show as one house automatically when this instance's room is in the area of a room or the adjoining room of another instance with more rooms (but not its leading room). source_problem.title: HC – {name}: heat source problem
source_problem.description:
The heat source of **{name}** shows a problem since {since}: **{problem}**.

Check the boiler (error code, gas, flame, relay). HC goes on regulating as well as it can. This entry clears itself as soon as the source is fine. For a notification use the blueprint that comes with HC.

circuit_problem.title: HC – {name}: mixing circuit watch
circuit_problem.description:
The **{name}** mixing circuit, since {since}: **{problem}**.

HC does not act on this, it only reports it. Check the PLC (pump enable, start delay), the mixing valve and its controller (an ESP, for example), and the tank's temperature. The entry clears itself once the circuit works again. The waiting times can be set in the circuit's settings, where the watch can also be switched off.
